definition: The basic unit of text that a language model processes, which may be a word, part of a word, or punctuation mark, produced by a tokenizer.
details: Language models don't operate directly on raw text; they operate on sequences of token IDs. The choice of tokenization scheme affects vocabulary size, sequence length, and how efficiently the model represents rare words.

explainer.lead: A token is the basic unit of text a language model processes, which may be a word, part of a word, or punctuation mark, produced by a tokenizer. It matters because models operate on token sequences, not raw text.

tiers.eli5: Like breaking a sentence into puzzle pieces the model can pick up, where a piece might be a whole word or just a bit of one.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers reason in tokens because the tokenization scheme affects vocabulary size, sequence length, and how efficiently rare words are represented. Pitfall: unusual words split into many tokens, inflating sequence length and cost.
tiers.paperLevel: The basic unit of text a language model processes, produced by a tokenizer; models operate on sequences of token IDs rather than raw text.

explainer.example: A rare word may be split into several subword tokens, so it occupies more of the sequence than a common word would.
